dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: A record-like inductive type carrying three real components. For tr, these components are denoted below by s, t, and e.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target universally quantifies over tr and uses its first, second, and third real components as the three successive rounded values s, t, and e.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: The function selecting the third real component of a LocalDef001 value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: LocalDef002 tr is e, the rounded result associated with the exact quantity y - t and the correction added to s in the equality s + e = x + y.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The function selecting the first real component of a LocalDef001 value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: LocalDef003 tr is s, assumed to be a nearest representable value to x + y and used in both conclusions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: The function selecting the second real component of a LocalDef001 value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: LocalDef004 tr is t, assumed to be a nearest representable value to the exact difference s - x.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef005 R a r means that r is R-representable and globally minimizes absolute error from a among all R-representable real candidates: R(r) and, for every real c, R(c) implies |a - r| ≤ |a - c|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It states that s is nearest representable to x + y, t is nearest representable to s - x, and e is nearest representable to y - t. It allows ties and specifies no tie-breaking rule.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: The constructor that forms a LocalDef001 value from three arbitrary real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It confirms that the triple type itself imposes no numerical invariant on s, t, and e; all constraints used by the theorem come from the explicit hypotheses.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It combines the exact equality s + e = x + y with the error bound |s - (x + y)| ≤ |y|. It also combines representability and global minimality inside each LocalDef005 hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Propositional equality between two values of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses the exact real-number identity s + e = x + y.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous-addition operation supplied by an HAdd instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the displayed real-number instance, every occurrence is ordinary real addition, including x + y and s + e.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous-subtraction operation supplied by an HSub instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the displayed real-number instance, it gives the ordinary real differences s - x, y - t, and s - (x + y), as well as the differences in the nearest-representable definition.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The less-than-or-equal relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real numbers it expresses both the global absolute-error comparisons in LocalDef005 and the final bound |s - (x + y)| ≤ |y|.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The inputs x and y, all three components s, t, and e, every representable candidate, and all exact or computed quantities are scalar real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard addition structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It resolves the additions in x + y, s + e, and real subtraction to standard real arithmetic.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: The additive-group structure on the real numbers, supplying zero, addition, negation, and subtraction laws.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the negation operation used by absolute value and supports the standard interpretation of all real differences.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard less-than-or-equal relation on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes every comparison in the proposition an ordinary real inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard real subtraction operation, defined by a - b = a + (-b).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the exact intermediate quantities s - x and y - t, the final error s - (x + y), and all absolute errors in LocalDef005.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard lattice structure on the real numbers, including maximum and minimum.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the maximum operation used to define |a| as max(a, -a), hence gives the standard real absolute values appearing throughout.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real number a, abs(a) is max(a, -a), the standard absolute value |a|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It measures every rounding error and appears in the final estimate |s - (x + y)| ≤ |y|.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: The homogeneous HAdd instance induced by an Add instance, so heterogeneous-addition notation applies the underlying addition operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instAdd, it ensures that all HAdd expressions in the target are standard addition of real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: The homogeneous HSub instance induced by a Sub instance, so heterogeneous-subtraction notation applies the underlying subtraction operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instSub, it ensures that all HSub expressions in the target are standard subtraction of real numbers.

binders: An arbitrary predicate R on the real numbers, interpreted as representability.
Arbitrary real numbers x and y.
An arbitrary triple tr of real numbers; write s for its first component, t for its second component, and e for its third component.
hypotheses: s is representable and is a global nearest representable real to the exact sum x + y: for every real c, if R(c), then |(x + y) - s| ≤ |(x + y) - c|.
The exact difference s - x is representable: R(s - x).
t is representable and is a global nearest representable real to the exact difference s - x: for every real c, if R(c), then |(s - x) - t| ≤ |(s - x) - c|.
The exact difference y - t is representable: R(y - t).
e is representable and is a global nearest representable real to the exact difference y - t: for every real c, if R(c), then |(y - t) - e| ≤ |(y - t) - c|.
conclusions: The exact equality s + e = x + y holds.
The absolute error in s as an approximation to x + y is bounded by |y|: |s - (x + y)| ≤ |y|.
mathematical_definitions: For a representability predicate R, define Near_R(a,r) to mean R(r) and ∀c ∈ Real, R(c) implies |a - r| ≤ |a - c|.
The three exact quantities supplied to the nearest-representable assumptions are a0 = x + y, a1 = s - x, and a2 = y - t.
The components satisfy Near_R(a0,s), Near_R(a1,t), and Near_R(a2,e), together with the additional assumptions R(x), R(a1), and R(a2).
All additions, subtractions, order comparisons, and absolute values are the standard operations on scalar real numbers.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every representability predicate R on the reals, every pair of real numbers x and y, and every real triple (s,t,e), suppose x is representable; s is a nearest representable value to x + y; the exact difference s - x is itself representable; t is a nearest representable value to s - x; the exact difference y - t is itself representable; and e is a nearest representable value to y - t. Then s + e equals x + y exactly, and the absolute error |s - (x + y)| is at most |y|.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The predicate R is completely arbitrary. The proposition does not encode a floating-point format, discreteness, finiteness, closure properties, rounding mode, precision, exponent range, exceptional values, or any other structure on representable numbers.
All quantities are scalar real numbers; there are no vectors, matrices, dimensions, or componentwise operations.
Each nearest-representable hypothesis asserts a global minimizer among all R-representable real candidates. Existence of such minimizers is assumed for the selected s, t, and e, not proved.
Nearest values need not be unique, because equality of errors is allowed and no tie-breaking rule is specified.

The assumptions that s - x and y - t are exactly representable are strong. Together with the nearest-representable hypotheses, they force zero error at the second and third stages, hence t = s - x and e = y - t.
The number y is not required to be representable.

The statement is a chain of implications. For any chosen R, x, y, and tr, it is automatically true if any required hypothesis fails; in particular, it is vacuous when the relevant nearest-representable values do not exist or when x is not representable.
No algorithm for computing s, t, or e is encoded. They are arbitrary triple components constrained only by the hypotheses.
